commits.edited_message:
don't preallocate manifests when parsing IDManifests (#2575)

Build manifest entries and the compressed string mapping incrementally, and keep the mapping lookup checked while the mapping is being built.

Signed-off-by: Peter Hillman <peterh@wetafx.co.nz>

Bound IDManifest uncompressed size and version-field read (#2572)

Reject implausible uncompressed sizes and short version fields before reading manifest data. Also hoist the mapped string index into a local after the existing index validation.

Signed-off-by: Peter Hillman <peterh@wetafx.co.nz>

coupling: The first edited commit changes the IDManifest compressed-string mapping from a vector pre-sized to stringList.size() to an incrementally built vector, and keeps its own lookup checked with vector::at. That representation is safe by itself. The second edited commit changes the existing lookup to hoist mapping[stringIndex] into a local after validating stringIndex only against stringList.size(); against the original pre-sized mapping that refactor is safe. Only when the two commits combine can a file declare two top-level strings but provide an RLE mapping for one, then use compressed string index 1: it passes the stringList bound but reads one element past the one-element mapping. A correct fix must reconcile the sparse mapping representation introduced by the first commit with the unchecked consumer changed by the second commit (for example, validate against mapping.size() or use a checked lookup); either commit viewed without the other appears to preserve correct maintenance behavior.
